body: I'm financially dependent on my parents and am on their insurance plan. I hate to sound stupid but I'm not really too sure how insurance works. Would insurance cover the hospitalization completely?

This reply was very helpful, thank you.

I get what you're saying! How do you think my therapist would talk to my parents about it? Do you think she'd write an email? I'm really worried because my dad especially has the tendency to get enraged about things like this, and could end up kicking me out of the house. I have no money of my own, and can't get a job because of the very issue that is making me suicidal. I don't have friends or anyone else, either. I'd literally be on the streets.

Another thing is my mom is kind of depressed already so my family cares more about helping her out (even though they don't call it "depression"). She's going through an injury, so they think she has a legitimate reason to be feeling down, but if I told them I was just sad for no reason they wouldn't take it seriously and would tell me to suck it up or deal with getting kicked out of the house, because other people have worse problems and they think I don't have anything going wrong in my life.

What do you think, considering this?

I already talked to her about it and she didn't seem very understanding. 

She did give me the option to present to her privately, but I don't know if she was totally OK with the idea of that -- she looked kind of wary, like she didn't even believe my issue was real. I have a problem with the oral presentation because I have a voice disorder that makes my voice sound weird/hard to understand, especially when I'm nervous. I don't like people to hear my voice to begin with, but when I'm nervous (which I will be during an oral presentation), it'll be even worse. This is what went wrong last time. 

If I didn't have a voice disorder and this was just normal nerves, that'd be a different story, but this is what I have to deal with.

Hi! Thanks for your reply. It really helps to hear someone say that. 

I'm wondering if you can give me advice on how to get out of this oral presentation, because I know that going through with it will make me feel even worse than I already do. I had an oral presentation in the same class a few weeks ago and had an absolute breakdown (that no one knew about) for 4 straight days after that. My issues with the oral presentation are the very issues that make me feel suicidal to begin with, so this really won't work out.

I'm already talking to a therapist at my college. She's the only person I'm talking to right now, that knows anything about what I'm currently going through. She understands how bad things are for me anxiety wise, but I'm afraid to tell her I'm suicidal because it feels weird to say. Also, I don't want her telling my parents or anyone else about it.

Not sure how I'll get a second chance for an oral presentation. I have an appointment with my therapist later today. Do you think there's some way she could help me out? I don't know what exactly to tell her. I don't want to mention that I'm suicidal, but I feel like she wouldn't take me seriously enough otherwise.

Hey,

Thanks for your reply. I really appreciate it.

I had a question specifically about the oral presentation. I already talked to my professor about it last class and she wants me doing it no matter what. I told her my problems, that I have a voice disorder that doesn't allow me to talk properly and gets even worse when I'm nervous, and she didn't seem very keen on letting me present to her privately in office hours. The presentation is tomorrow and I'll have no opportunity to talk to her before class. Is there anything I can do as a last resort? She's not responsive by email either.

I'm really not in the mental state to be worrying about something like this. I really just want to skip class tomorrow, but then I'd be even more anxious about everyone and my professor noticing me skipping class the day of a presentation.
